The bullet separator is a standard middle dot (•).

clarified_description: The Pixie sandbox changelog page will display an estimated reading time for each entry. This estimate is calculated on the client side based on the word count of the entry description, using a rate of 200 words per minute. The reading time will be rendered on the same line as the entry title, separated by a bullet character, using small, muted text. This change is strictly a UI enhancement and does not involve modifications to the underlying data source or the RSS feed.

constraints.detail: Implementation must be restricted to the client-side components; no changes to the data schema or server-side routes are permitted.

must: The system shall calculate reading time based on the word count of the entry description.
The system shall use a calculation rate of 200 words per minute.
The system shall round the result up to the nearest whole minute.
The system shall display a minimum reading time of '1 min read'.
The system shall render the reading time on the same line as the entry title.
The system shall separate the title and the reading time with a bullet separator (e.g., •).
The system shall render the reading time using small, muted text styles.
The system shall include a test to verify the reading time calculation and rendering logic.
outcome: Users can see an estimated reading time next to each changelog entry to help them decide if they want to read the update.
rationale: The user requested a client-side calculation to avoid the overhead and complexity of updating the data layer and the RSS feed. The constraints on rounding (up) and minimum value (1 min) ensure a consistent and predictable user experience even for very short entries.

risks.mitigation: Ensure a robust word-counting regex is used to handle whitespace and punctuation correctly.
risks.title: Calculation accuracy

should: The system shall only display the reading time if the description contains more than 10 words.

criteria: Time is displayed next to the title
